name: Rattlespike
body:
Rattlespike
CR 1

XP 400
NE Small undead
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +0

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 12, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 13 (3d8)
Fort +1, Ref +2, Will +3
DR 5/bludgeoning; Immune cold, undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +5 (1d4+2), slam +5 (1d3+2)
Ranged bone spike +4 (1d3+2)

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 13, Con —, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 10
Base Atk +2; CMB +3; CMD 14

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bone Spikes (Ex)

A rattlespike is covered in razor-sharp, protruding bone spikes from which it gets its name. Its slam attack deals both piercing and bludgeoning damage. A rattlespike can launch one of its spikes as a ranged attack with a range of 20 feet. A creature that strikes a rattlespike with a natural weapon or attempts to grapple it sustains 1d6 piercing damage. Succeeding at a DC 13 Reflex save halves the damage. Save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

ECOLOGY

Environment any Organization solitary, pair, or pack (3-9)
Treasure none

Rattlespikes are skeletal undead roughly the size of a large dog. Their skulls may be animal or humanoid, but they are always quadruped, mindless and riddled with jagged, shattered bones that function as spikes that give them their name. Bone spikes work mainly defensively, but can also be launched at targets by the creature.

Rattlespikes are a favorite of small-time necromancers, because they require only animal bones and can be made with imperfect, mismatched and damaged material, which normally can’t be used to create fully functional skeletons and zombies.

An average rattlespike is between 3 and 4 feet long and weighs around 15 pounds. The “rattle” part of their name comes from both the characteristic clank of bone shards colliding with each other and from the curious jitters that the creatures often display, just as if they were cold or scared, though it’s obviously not the case.
